Subject: Capacity entitlement — thermals & slice mapping for NexaGen late-stage

Team,

NexaGen (NXG-8273) is moving to signatures this week; legal expects PO within 7 days. They want a firm picture of how we’ll map the requested capacity to our fleet and any thermal/power constraints that could affect start-of-service. Quick ask: can infra confirm true availability for a 40-GPU N1 slice (A100 equivalent) for initial prod ramp, plus a 20-GPU burst lane for the first 30 days?

Concrete items I need by EOD tomorrow:
- Physical rack mapping: which racks/availability zones would host the N1 slice?
- Thermal headroom: are any candidate racks thermally constrained (rack inlet temp / power budget concerns)?
- Eviction tolerance: what's the recommended eviction policy if we need to spread across zones?
- Ops hold: recommend duration for a provisional capacity hold (48/72 hours?) and any commercial implications (credits or commit language).

Attaching: NexaGen_MTL_capacity_request.xlsx (requested sizing) and deal summary.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity entitlement — thermals & slice mapping for NexaGen late-stage

Marissa —

Thanks, this is a helpful summary. Quick technical readout from ops after an initial sweep: 
- Us-west-2: we can satisfy a 40-GPU N1 slice but not from a single contiguous rack. Best-fit is racks R3-R6 across two pod clusters (R3/4 have ~8% thermal headroom left; R5/6 about ~14%).
- Us-east-1: stronger headroom (20%+ on candidate racks) but will introduce cross-region egress for snapshot/failover traffic.

Recommendation: spread N1 across us-west-2 (primary) and us-east-1 (secondary) with KV cache affinity pinned to primary to avoid cold-starts. For the 20-GPU burst lane, we can place it in us-east-1 and advertise a 200ms extra tail latency on burst calls until warmed.

Eviction policy: preemptible batch instances for non-critical jobs; pinned user-facing slices marked with "no-evict" priority. If we must reduce contiguous allocation, we prefer graceful draining (30s token stream drain) over hard preempt.

Suggested provisional hold: 72 hours to allow procurement + rack reservation to be processed; shorter holds (48h) increase risk of scramble for specific SKU racks.

Attaching: rack_map_south.png (ops rack map snapshot).

- Karthik
Sr. Infra Lead — Serving Runtime

Marissa / Karthik —

From a sales/contracting perspective: NexaGen is asking for a "capacity assurance" clause in the SOW (30-day runway guarantee). If ops recommends 72-hour provisional hold, commercial prefers we layer that with a 30-day soft-commit tied to a nominal monthly minimum so they have runway for onboarding. Two points: 
1) Do we want to offer a 30-day soft-commit at a small discount in exchange for a firm onboarding date?
2) If we go cross-region, we need to confirm any cost delta and surface that in the quote (egress, cross-region replica costs).

If legal/finance are okay, I'll draft language: 72-hour provisional hold + 30-day soft-commit (non-binding but prioritized placement) with X% credit if we fail to provide the slice on the agreed date.

Ben

Redwood Inference

Evan / NexaGen team — looping you in with a short path forward so expectations are clear on both sides.

Internal summary and ask completed:
- Ops can place the 40-GPU N1 slice across us-west-2 (primary) and us-east-1 (secondary) with the recommended KV cache affinity to primary.
- Thermal constraints exist on R3-R4 (us-west-2); we will split to avoid hot spots.
- Ops recommends a 72-hour provisional hold to lock candidate racks while procurement issues PO.

Commercial proposal (Ben): 72-hour provisional hold + 30-day prioritized placement (soft-commit) included in our onboarding plan. Pricing note: cross-region placement will add an estimated 6% to monthly unit costs (egress + replica overhead). Ben will include exact line items in the quote.

Next steps: 
1) Evan: confirm PO ETA and whether NexaGen needs a DocuSign SOW or a PO first.
2) Ben: please draft the provisional-hold language and the 30-day soft-commit clause.
3) Karthik/ops: run a final cross-region placement test on R5 to validate KV affinity behavior; capture any perf delta.

I am opening a 72-hour provisional rack hold effective now. Please keep this thread for any follow-ups or evidence requested by NexaGen procurement.

Thanks all —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
